title: Gaussian noise integral factorization
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho,s\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $s\ne0$ and $s^2+\rho^2=1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ and $x\in\mathbb R^n$. With $Y$ distributed according to the product standard Gaussian measure, one has
\[\mathbb E\bigl[f(\rho x+sY)\bigr]=\left(\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{\sqrt{2\pi s^2}}\right)^n e^{\|x\|^2/2}\,\mathbb E\left[f(Y)\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_i\left(\frac{x_i}{s}-\frac{\rho y_i}{s}\right)^2\right)\right],\]
where the expectation on the right is over $Y$.
